assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalyzed C-N coupling turned aryl amine construction from a harsh, substrate-limited problem into a routine, general operation. It is among the most used reactions in medicinal chemistry and process chemistry, with a clear mechanistic rationale (ligand design driving oxidative addition and reductive elimination). This is exactly the general-method impact I value, and it builds on but is distinct from the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig developed the general catalytic systems and ligand families independently and in parallel; Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work is a genuine precursor but did not deliver a general method. A two-person prize is clean and fair.
assessment.maturity: Over thirty years of independent confirmation and industrial adoption; recognition is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: The relation to the 2010 Nobel Prize for Pd cross-coupling may weigh on the committee as overlap.
Kosugi's precursor priority could be raised; I have not independently verified the historical details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Selective C-H functionalization changes retrosynthetic logic by treating C-H bonds as functional groups. Ligand-enabled and template-directed control of site selectivity made it practical, and it is already used in late-stage functionalization and in total synthesis, which fits an efficiency-in-synthesis criterion.
assessment.attribution: Yu (ligand-accelerated directing-group and distal C-H activation), Sanford (Pd(II/IV) catalysis) and Hartwig (borylation, with Smith) made distinct decisive contributions; Daugulis and Smith are also credible. Three is a sensible ceiling but the selection is somewhat arbitrary.
assessment.maturity: Broad uptake in academic and increasingly industrial settings, though industrial scale use is less routine than cross-coupling; some strategies remain substrate-specific. Timely, bordering on slightly early.
uncertainties: Several competing subfields (directed, undirected, borylation, distal) make a coherent citation difficult.
Hartwig is also credited on B038, which could create allocation conflicts.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis opened radical and open-shell reactivity under mild conditions and became a standard tool across academic and pharmaceutical labs. It added a new activation mode, combined with nickel and organocatalysis, and has a large footprint in late-stage functionalization.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread over many people (seven credited); MacMillan, Yoon and Stephenson published the landmark 2008 and 2009 papers. MacMillan already shared the 2021 prize for organocatalysis, which complicates a repeat recognition. Konig, Fukuzumi, Nicewicz and Melchiorre made real contributions.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed and widely adopted, but the field is still evolving and the Ru/Ir-to-organic-dye and energy-transfer branches are in flux.
uncertainties: MacMillan's earlier prize may lead the committee to prefer other configurations.
Priority among early photoredox contributors (including pre-2008 work) is not fully settled in my knowledge.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native chemical ligation made total chemical synthesis and semisynthesis of proteins routine and gave chemists access to homogeneous, modified proteins. It is a genuinely new chemical bond-forming concept (chemoselective thioester-thiol exchange with S-to-N acyl shift) with extensive applications, including in therapeutic protein research.
assessment.attribution: Kent and Dawson introduced NCL; Muir developed expressed protein ligation and semisynthesis. Danishefsky, Brik and Liu are significant but later or more applied. The three-person set is reasonable.
assessment.maturity: Well established for roughly 30 years and still widely used; recognition is timely. Impact is concentrated in chemical biology and a specialist community rather than ubiquitous.
uncertainties: Some of the impact is at the border with biology, and the sharing of credit between ligation and semisynthesis needs care.
Whether the committee views it as a general chemistry method is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Frustrated Lewis pairs showed that sterically encumbered acid-base pairs activate H2 and other small molecules without a transition metal, a conceptually simple and surprising new reactivity pattern that led to metal-free hydrogenation catalysis.
assessment.attribution: Stephan (initial discovery of reversible H2 activation, 2006) and Erker (a distinct group of FLP systems and reactions) are the natural pairing. Welch and Stephan's contribution is core; Erker's is substantial, though the supplied credit is limited to these two.
assessment.maturity: Strong confirmation across many groups, but practical impact on synthesis is still modest compared with transition-metal catalysis; the field is perhaps a few years early for the prize.
uncertainties: Synthetic application has been limited, so I weigh it below the cross-coupling and C-H candidates.
I have not verified the finer priority questions about pre-2006 related work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Isolation of stable carbenes changed the understanding of reactive intermediates and provided N-heterocyclic carbenes that became ubiquitous ligands and organocatalysts, notably in olefin metathesis catalysts and in organocatalysis.
assessment.attribution: Arduengo isolated the first crystalline NHC (1991), and Bertrand isolated the earlier phosphinocarbene and later cyclic alkyl amino carbenes. Nolan, Rovis and Bode are important for applications, and a two-name configuration is cleaner.
assessment.maturity: Decades of confirmation and wide uptake; the impact partly overlaps with the 2005 metathesis prize, which may reduce urgency.
uncertainties: The committee might see this as ligand-level rather than field-defining discovery.
The relationship of the Bertrand 1988 carbene work to Arduengo's priority may be contentious.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Metal-directed self-assembly of discrete cages and capsules gives programmable, well-defined supramolecular architectures with host-guest, catalytic and structural applications. The conceptual simplicity of coordination-driven assembly is attractive, though my interest is in what it enables chemically.
assessment.attribution: Fujita, Stang and Raymond made early decisive contributions to coordination-driven cage design; Nitschke and Ward developed more complex cages later. Three is a plausible configuration but borders on arbitrary.
assessment.maturity: Mature as a field, with continuing growth, but the practical impact beyond supramolecular chemistry is still limited.
uncertainties: Practical use in synthesis and industry is modest.
The 2016 and 1987 supramolecular prizes may reduce the case.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Phosphoramidite chemistry made automated, reliable oligonucleotide synthesis possible and underpins sequencing primers, PCR, gene synthesis and nucleic-acid therapeutics. It is a classic enabling synthetic method with enormous downstream use.
assessment.attribution: Caruthers developed phosphoramidite chemistry and the associated solid-phase approach; Hood is credited mainly for automation of the synthesizer and is not a decisive contributor to the chemistry. I would propose Caruthers alone, accepting that this leaves out instrument development.
assessment.maturity: Method is about forty years old and thoroughly proven; the question is whether a prize now is timely or very late, and its prior recognition status in other awards is not something I can verify.
uncertainties: Whether Hood's contribution is decisive for the chemistry is doubtful.
Opening position is low confidence relative to the top candidates because of the long delay and credit complexity.
